standard_prerequisites.name: Flows, orbit closures and finite oscillation stability
standard_prerequisites.statement: A flow is an action of a topological group on a compact space, the orbit closure of a point is the closure of its orbit, and a fixed point is a point the group does not move; a finite family of functions is finitely oscillation stable at a point when for every finite set of group elements and every precision there is a point of the orbit on which all the functions of the family vary by less than the precision. The author's own definitions are the ones used by the counted statement and proof.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted proposition is the pointwise criterion that identifies the existence of a fixed point in an orbit closure with the finite oscillation stability of the functions evaluated at the point, and the article uses it as the first step of its fixed point theorems.

core_obligations: Forward direction, set-up: fix a finite family of continuous functions, a finite set of group elements and a precision, and take a fixed point in the orbit closure (source line 242).

Forward direction, approximation: by continuity of the functions of the family there is a point of the orbit close enough to the fixed point that every function of the family, evaluated at every group element of the finite set, is within half the precision of its value at the fixed point; since the fixed point is fixed, this gives the variation bound (source line 242).

Forward direction, conclusion: combine the two estimates through a point of the orbit to obtain the same value of the function at two group elements, which is the finite oscillation stability required (source lines 242-248).

Converse direction, construction: define, for each finite family, finite set of group elements and precision, the set of points of the orbit closure on which every function of the family varies by at most the precision along the finite set of group elements (source lines 250-253).

Converse direction, finite intersection property: these sets are closed, and the hypothesis of finite oscillation stability puts a point of the orbit in every finite intersection, so the family has the finite intersection property (source line 255).
Converse direction, conclusion: the intersection of the family is non-empty by compactness, and every point of it is fixed, which gives the fixed point in the orbit closure (source line 255).

proof_roadmap.step: Forward direction: from a fixed point in the orbit closure, approximate it by a point of the orbit so that all the functions of a finite family agree within the precision along the finite set of group elements, then combine the two estimates into the variation bound.
Converse direction: for each finite family, finite set of group elements and precision, define the set of points of the orbit closure on which the family varies by at most the precision.
Show the family of these closed sets has the finite intersection property by finite oscillation stability, conclude that its intersection is non-empty, and observe that its points are fixed.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 doi:10.5802/ahl.16 中**无源 label** 的 Proposition（源 233-240 行，按其第一枚举项的 label 2.2.1 识别；证明 241-256 行，24 行）：设 G 作用在紧空间 X 上、x∈X，则「轨道闭包 G·x 含不动点」⇔「对每个有限族 F⊂C(X)，{f_x} 有限振荡稳定」。两个方向都**自带构造**，不是引用链：正方向用**连续性把不动点附近的轨道点拉过来**（取 g·x 使 |f(h·g·x)−f(h·y)|<ε/2，再利用 y 不动）得到双估计并合成 |f_x(hg)−f_x(h'g)|<ε；反方向构造一族**闭集** A_{F,H,ε}={y∈G·x 闭包 : ∀f∀h |f(h·y)−f(y)|≤ε}，由假设它有**有限交性质**，再用紧性取交非空，最后验证交中的点都是不动点。难点在于两个方向的「近似—紧性」配对，以及反方向要把「有限振荡稳定」正确读成有限交性质。原文位置：正方向 242-248 行，反方向 250-255 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's Proposition at source lines 233-240 together with its proof at source lines 241-256, a straight adjacent pairing in the source file. The statement environment carries no source label, so the card is keyed by the label of its first enumerated item, 2.2.1, which is the article's own printed number for that item and the handle the rest of the article uses for it. The source is the publisher version of the article in Annales Henri Lebesgue 2 (2019), pages 149-185, DOI 10.5802/ahl.16, released under CC BY 4.0.

The gate was run on the narrowed interval 236-256, which starts at the line of the enumerated item, because the statement's own label sits three lines inside the statement environment and the gate refuses a start more than two lines above it. The card records the complete environment 233-240, which is the only way the enumerated list renders; this is the same statement/label arrangement as the earlier card of this source whose label also sits on an enumerated item.

The licence evidence used here is the observation file kept with the source, license-observation.json, which records the licence as CC BY 4.0, points at the inherited publisher-version evidence and states that the landing page displays no licence line; the underlying evidence files are the same ones the earlier cards of this source rely on. No acceptance record is written anywhere.

The retained proof uses only the numbering of the two enumerated items of its own statement and the definitions of the section: it contains no pointer to another statement and no citation, so this card declares no navigation pointer and needs no bibliography entry. The equation numbers that appear in the proof are the article's own references into this same statement and are displayed as tags by the assembler.

The retained preamble is the source's editorial preamble with three omissions only: the class line, which the assembler supplies; the page geometry; and the fontspec block with its explicit font files, which would fight the forced xelatex engine. Everything else, including the theorem declarations under the shared counter and the whole macro block, is retained verbatim.

The card makes the excerpt display the numbers the article prints for its own objects, because the retained proof quotes them: the top level of the statement's enumeration is redefined in this card's own copy of the preamble to display 2.2.1 and 2.2.2, which are the handles the proof uses, and the section counter is set to two so that the displayed formula of the proof carries the number the article gives it, which the equation counter at ten produces. Revision r002 set those counters but left the enumeration showing its default labels, and revision r003 adds the redefinition so the labels and the cross-references agree. The theorem-like environment of the statement is renumbered by the assembler as 2.1, the first of its section; nothing in the retained span refers to it by number, since the proof quotes only the two enumerated items.
